(a) Only the gold, SevenZFile.isDirectoryByHeader, makes the directory decision. It reports the PAX header ('x' flag, name ending in '/') as a directory, which breaks its "@return whether the entry represents a directory". Hop 1 only answers for entries created from a file, and hops 2-4 just pass the entry on.

(b) Each hop's javadoc matches its code.

(c) Two one-line pre-filters pass the trigger and the full suite. One is in hop 4: `!entry.isPaxHeader() && !entry.isGlobalPaxHeader() && ...`. The other is in TarArchiveInputStream.isDirectory: `!currEntry.isPaxHeader() && ...`. Both leave the gold's contract broken, so I count them as bypasses, not competing repairs.

(d) No leakage. The lie describes a check on the entry's mode, which the code never does, and it does not name PAX.

(e) The recipe holds. There are five calls from the facade to the gold. The hosts match hosts_hop_order exactly (largest5 regime, TarArchiveEntry excluded). The facade body is `isDirectoryEntry(this, linkFlag)`. There is one appended lie. The gold's javadoc says nothing about the omitted step. test.patch is empty.

(g) The C10i rules hold. No visibility was widened, no type was added, no reflection is used, and the facade's signature is unchanged.

(f) The convention is pinned outside the gold. getNextTarEntry and paxHeaders read a PAX header's data as records. putArchiveEntry sets a directory's size to 0, while writePaxHeaders still writes data. shouldBeReplaced replaces '/' in PAX header names.

Notes for the reviewer, none of them grounds for rejection:
- Any pass-through hop can pre-filter this fault. The declared hop-2 alternative filters only the global 'g' flag, not the 'x' flag the trigger uses, so gate G9 never tries the pre-filter that works.
- The existing comment in shouldBeReplaced describes the variant's behaviour as the entry's known behaviour, so a reader could blame TarArchiveInputStream instead.
- The omission is the same as the real Compress-38 bug.

Hop 1 and hops 2-4 do what their docs say, and the facade lie has no effect on single-line text.

(b) No hop's javadoc contradicts its code.

(c) Three non-gold edits pass the trigger, the ownership tests and the full suite. All are bypasses, none competing: hop 1 calling the segmented writeRaw(text,0,len) makes hops 2-5 dead; hop 3 and hop 4 passing a fresh array the size of the text go against the "char buffer of the generator" docs and make the gold's buffering dead.

(f) The convention is pinned outside the gold by writeRaw(String,int,int), writeRawLong and _flushBuffer, which all reset to index 0.

(g) Nothing is widened, no type is added, there is no reflection, the facade signature is unchanged and no test is edited.

T3.why: There is no closed set of parallel siblings, two-member pair or named class in the text with one member left out. The flush test is the only per-element treatment.

T4.quote: "whenever the next code point does not fit in the buffer, the chars gathered so far are passed to the generator first" vs body: "if (filled + count > buf.length) { gen.writeRaw(buf, 0, filled); } filled += Character.toChars(c, buf, filled);"

No allowed instance method can carry the C10i recipe validly.

1. getQualifiedName and isQualifiedName have no one-line omission that exactly one existing test catches. They have 142 and 42 production call sites, and every behaviour change tested either fails many tests (61, 9, 204, 12) or none (0). Gate G5 cannot pass.

2. getSourceOffset has one production caller, JSError.getNodeSourceOffset, which nothing calls. Its only omission with a single trigger is the unknown-line guard (lineno == -1 -> -1), which NodeTest::testInvalidSourceOffset alone catches. That is a guard on a scalar the receiver exposes (node.getLineno() is public). Any of hops 1-4 can pre-filter it with a one-line edit, such as `return node.getLineno() == -1 ? -1 : Next.hop(node);`. That edit passes the trigger and the full suite, because mutant A's only failing test is the trigger. It is also consistent with every documented contract on the path and with the evidence: JSError's "-1 if the offset is unknown", and SourceMap.addMapping, which pins exactly this caller-side guard (`sourceFile == null || node.getLineno() < 0`).

So the fault breaks BUILD_BRIEF's fault rule (an iteration or decision "whose effect no caller can pre-filter or recover"). The gold also cannot be the single owner (W13): the pre-filter is a competing repair under AUDIT_BRIEF (c), not a bypass, and G9 or the auditor would reject it. The computation is a ten-line scalar with no iteration, so no restructuring moves the decision out of reach of the hops. Every other omission in getSourceOffset fails no test: without the file-null guard, the -1 position still exits at the line guard, and a decode-based variant gives MIN_VALUE+4095 < 0 on SimpleSourceFile.

Secondary obstacle: on Closure's 2-space indentation, the seeded anchors land in nested classes, and only 3 of the 12 hosts in the 1500 pool take an outer-class hop (see host_notes).

**setInteriorGap.** Its computation is a range guard (which stays in the facade), a change test, a field write and a notification. Only the field write is observable: the only test that reaches it is testEquals, and no test registers a listener. The value written is a pass-through of `percent`. Any one-line omission that changes the stored value removes the line that adopts the requested value. That leaves either:
- a result local that is never updated (initialised from `current` and returned unchanged), with `requested` read only in the change test; or
- code that does not compile (the omitted line is the return).

Either way, a gold whose javadoc says it applies the requested value contradicts its body. That is T4, and T2 under the checklist's doubt rule. It is also exactly the visibly broken idiom the brief warns against. Omitting the change test or the notification is not observed by any test.

**setExplodePercent.** Its computation is a null-key guard (which stays in the facade), lazy creation of a map that the constructor always creates, one put and a notification. Only the put is observable (via equals). Omitting it leaves `key` and `percent` unused in the gold, which is T1. Omitting the lazy creation is never executed and is a dead branch (T2c). Omitting the notification is not observed by any test.

**Common to both.**
- Neither has an iteration or a special-case decision. There is no per-element core to put in hop 5, so hops 1-4 would be empty pass-throughs.
- Any pass-through hop could trivially recover the stored value by returning the requested value or putting the entry itself, so the single-owner rule cannot hold.
- Adding a richer computation, such as change filtering for setExplodePercent or normalisation of the value, would change behaviour, and is not allowed.
- The facade must write its private field. Doing that through a V1 write-back after a hop that calls `notifyListeners` would also notify listeners before the field changes.

sample() is pure arithmetic with no decision in it: it draws z_i = random.nextGaussian() for each dimension, computes samplingMatrix.operate(z) (sequential row sums), and adds the means. Two existing tests reach it, and between them they catch every change to its output.

1. MultivariateNormalMixtureModelDistributionTest::testSampling compares 100 seeded samples with stored values to 1e-16, which is about bit-exact. Its component 0 has the same parameters as the other test's distribution (mu {-1.5, 2}, sigma {{2,-1.1},{-1.1,2}}), so any change to the output on those parameters fails it.
2. MultivariateNormalDistributionTest::testSampling checks the mean and covariance of 500,000 samples with tolerance 1e-2. The statistical noise is about 0.004. The omissions available in any split of the chain are:
   - dropping the mean term moves the mean by 1.5 or 2;
   - dropping any product term or Gaussian draw moves a covariance entry by S_ij^2 >= 0.165, since every entry of the sampling matrix is at least 0.4 in magnitude;
   - a loop bound or write omission is visibly frozen (T2) and changes the output just as much.
   Each of these is far outside the tolerance.

So every quiet omission fails both tests. I confirmed this empirically on the scratch copy:
- with the mean addition omitted, both tests fail;
- with the last Gaussian draw omitted, both tests fail.

Only a change that preserves the distribution exactly would fail the mixture test alone:
- a permutation or sign flip of z, or the transpose of the symmetric sampling matrix;
- an ulp-level reordering.

None of these is a one-line omission. They are substitutions or reorderings, and they would need the correct gold to contain a contrived compensating step, which would itself leave a local trace. The original computation has no special-case step (special value, boundary, pairing or reset) whose omission is confined to inputs only one test exercises. The allowed candidate list has only this method. This is the batch-9 pre-registered UNBUILDABLE kind "no single-trigger omission".

CONFIRMED. Audit file: /Users/shawnli/Desktop/Honours/defects4j/.claude/worktrees/strict-depth-experiment-run-524113/supervisor_pipeline_runs/weaker-model-v1/construction/mainrun/audits/MI-JacksonDatabind-2.json.
(a) Only SerializerProvider.copyBinaryContent allocates the copy and moves bytes. On {1..7} it returns {1,...,6,0}, which breaks its documented contract ("the len bytes starting at offset, in order"). Every hop above it only forwards the arguments.
(b) Each hop's javadoc ("copy of the section") matches its delegating code.
(c) No competing repair. Rounding len up at hop 4 fails (it reads past the input). Two hop edits pass the full suite, and both are bypasses: hop 1 using Arrays.copyOfRange, and hop 3 padding the input then truncating the result.
(d) Names are neutral. The lie describes a base64 round trip and does not name the omitted tail copy.

T1.why: All three parameters take part in the main computation: data and offset in the copy reads, and len in the allocation and the loop bound.

T2.why: The only locals are result, which is written and returned, and i, which the loop advances with i += 3; there is no dead or no-op branch.

T3.why: The three copy lines (i, i+1, i+2) are one stride pattern; the closure rule does not make the leftover bytes after the last full triple a member of a closed set.

T4.quote: the len bytes of data that start at index offset ... @return Newly allocated array that contains the bytes of the section vs. while (i + 3 <= len) { ... i += 3; }
T4.why: The javadoc names a concrete count (all len bytes), but the loop guard visibly stops before the last len % 3 bytes and no line copies them, so for any len that is not a multiple of 3 the result leaves those slots at zero. This could be read as a general description the body does address (the Not-T4 exclusion), but I am unsure, and the brief counts that doubt as a trace.

T2.why: result is written and returned; i is the loop cursor, is advanced by "i += 3" inside the loop, and indexes live writes; no branch is dead.

build.reason:
Nothing to split into a five-hop chain with a quiet single-owner gold.

(1) The facade does no work once per call that a chain could carry. Its computation is a per-evaluation adapter: an anonymous ParametricUnivariateRealFunction wrapping Gaussian.Parametric that turns NotStrictlyPositiveException into +infinity. The optimizer calls it inside CurveFitter.fit through the private TheoreticalValuesFunction and the private optimizer field.
- Hops are public static methods called once, and they may not create a new class, anonymous class or nested type (addendum, not-allowed list). So the adapter cannot move into hops 1-5.
- No existing public type composes or guards a ParametricUnivariateRealFunction. The only implementers are Gaussian.Parametric, HarmonicOscillator.Parametric and PolynomialFitter's.
- The fitting itself is reachable only through the public CurveFitter.fit(f, guess) or fit(maxEval, f, guess), because the optimizer and the observation list are private to CurveFitter.
- What a once-per-call chain can therefore receive is (receiver, f, the 3-element initialGuess). It can only pass them through to fitter.fit. That gives no per-element core for hop 5 and no omission site that preserves behaviour; any copy or normalisation loop over the guess or the result would add computation the original does not have, and would break all six fit tests.

(2) The only alternative is to route the adapter's value() (and gradient()) through the chain, so it runs once per evaluation. That breaks the C10i facade shape: the facade would keep the adapter, a second inline evaluation path and the fit(f, initialGuess) call, instead of guard + state gathering + one call to hop 1. It still has no single owner:
- the only behaviour that exactly one existing test (testMath519) depends on is the sigma <= 0 to +infinity guard;
- that guard is a decision on a raw parameter, p[2], which every hop receives;
- so a one-line `if (p[2] <= 0) return Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY;` at any of hops 1-4, or a catch at a caller, repairs the trigger consistently with quiet hop docs. This violates BUILD_BRIEF's "a decision whose effect no caller can pre-filter or recover" and the single-owner rule (W13).
- No other omission isolates one test: the per-component Gaussian formula, gradient and fallbacks are exercised by all six reaching tests on positive sigma.

GaussianFitter.fit(double[]) is the record's only allowed candidate, so no other facade could be tried.
